newsitem.title: USA: Central Newspapers backs '96 EPS view.
newsitem.headline: Central Newspapers backs '96 EPS view.

text.p: Central Newspapers Inc is comfortable with the upper end of the $2.30 to $2.35 range of earnings per share estimates for 1996, chief financial officer Thomas MacGillivray said in prepared remarks to a media conference in New York.
MacGillivray spoke Thursday to analysts. A text of his remarks was received here today.
The executive also said assuming newsprint prices remained stable, "the current First Call (earnings estimate) range of $2.75 to $2.80 appears within reach at this time" for 1997.
For 1996, he said total revenues should be up about 6-1/2 percent for the year. Indianapolis, Ind.-based Central posted revenues of $579.9 million in 1995.

MacGillivray, in his remarks, said the company was changing its newspaper distribution practice in Indianapolis, going to an agency system. As a result, he said the company expects a workforce reduction charge of $2 million to $3 million to be spread over the first two quarters of 1997.
Central Newspaper executives were not immediately available to elaborate.

Concerning the company's 1996 expectations, MacGillivray said, "The top of this range ($2.30 to $2.35) would represent a 12 percent increase from the $2.10 we earned a year ago, excluding special charges."

MacGillivray told analysts that, as previously disclosed, 1996 full year results will include $5.5 million of special charges, $4.2 million of which are for the impairment of the company's old Phoenix newspapers headquarters and some malfunctioning equipment in Phoenix and $1.2 million for workforce reductions.
For 1997, he said the company expects total revenues will be up between five and six percent. Central said newsprint prices could firm by the second half of 1997.

MacGillivray also said in his remarks that since April, when the newspaper company authorized a buyback of up to one million shares in a three-year period, it has repurchased about 490,000 shares at an average price of $36.50.
This brings the company's current outstanding shares down to about 26.4 million, he added.
Central Newspapers was trading at 41-3/4, up 1/4.
